question.prompt: David drives from his home to the airport to catch a flight. He drives \(35\) miles in the first hour, but realizes that he will be \(1\) hour late if he continues at this speed. He increases his speed by \(15\) miles per hour for the rest of the way to the airport and arrives \(30\) minutes early. How many miles is the airport from his home?

solutions.explanation:
Changing from arriving \(1\) hour late to arriving \(30\) minutes early saves \(1.5\) hours. The first hour is the same in both travel plans, so all this saving occurs on the remaining journey.

His new speed is \(35+15=50\) miles per hour. Let \(x>0\) be the remaining distance in miles after the first hour. Since time equals distance divided by speed,
\[
\frac{x}{35}-\frac{x}{50}=\frac32.
\]
Both speeds are positive, so these denominators are nonzero. Multiplying by \(350\), the least common multiple of the denominators, gives
\[
10x-7x=525,
\qquad x=175.
\]
Including the first \(35\) miles, the airport is
\[
35+175=\boxed{210\text{ miles}}
\]
from his home, choice C. At this distance, continuing at \(35\) miles per hour would take \(6\) hours altogether, while the faster plan takes \(4.5\) hours. A scheduled arrival \(5\) hours after departure gives exactly the stated lateness and earliness.
solutions.title: Compare the remaining travel times

solutions.explanation:
After the first hour, David has already driven \(35\) miles. The two possible speeds for the remaining distance are \(35\) and \(50\) miles per hour. The faster plan changes his arrival from \(1\) hour late to \(30\) minutes early, so it saves \(1.5\) hours.

For the same distance, travel times are inversely proportional to speeds. Thus the slower and faster remaining times have ratio
\[
50:35=10:7.
\]
Their difference is \(3\) equal parts, corresponding to \(1.5\) hours, so each part is \(0.5\) hour. The faster remaining time is therefore
\[
7\cdot0.5=3.5\text{ hours}.
\]
At \(50\) miles per hour, the remaining distance is \(50\cdot3.5=175\) miles. Adding the first \(35\) miles gives \(\boxed{210\text{ miles}}\), choice C.
solutions.title: Use the ratio of travel times
